name: Abdiel
role: The one seraph in Satan's own legions who refuses the rebellion and alone returns to fight for Heaven
description: Category B (real but thin precedent), heavily Miltonic in dramatic function. The name (Hebrew, 'servant of God') does appear in later Jewish kabbalistic literature (the Zohar Chadash, Yitro 39.4, and related Raziel-tradition angelology) -- real named-angel sources, but strictly post-biblical Jewish mysticism, centuries removed from any independent 'loyal rebel-who-recants' narrative. The dramatic role -- lone dissenting conscience inside Satan's ranks -- has no known precedent and is substantially Miltonic invention (D) grafted onto a borrowed angelic name (B). See docs/milton/character-catalog.md §V.
narrative_function: Publicly denounces Satan's rebellion in Book V, then alone crosses back to Heaven's side before the War in Heaven begins.
